cases.purpose: Exact authority request fields and SHA-256; inspect deny/allow and verify a mocked allow starts a same-UID owned child with its status.
cases.oracle: The original obligations, published x86-64 UAPI layouts and the independent SHA-256 wire encoder described by tests/sol-doas-check.py. A controlled stateful peer checks exact argv, target, relevant environment and request digest; an actual private child under the fixture UID supplies its own exit status and records identity. The authority is synthetic and cannot establish real kernel authorization or privilege transitions.
cases.comparison: Seccomp redirects the exact device open to a private memfd and handles only that fd. Setup drives the peer with an independent Python UAPI encoder, executes the owned child on a valid handle, and verifies a tampered request digest is rejected. Each case retains raw input/output ioctl bytes, argv/env blobs, expected and actual digest, decision order, child identity/status, stderr and stdout. A narrowly scoped synthetic-success PR_SET_DUMPABLE(0) reply is logged where auth open uses it. Denied, auth-required and failed-reset branches must never start the child. An allow must start the actual harmless child and preserve its status. Listener bootstrap is precompiled and sends its listener before supervised operations; diagnostic stage files record the handoff. The source-review ownership and embedded-payload guard repairs are included.
